subject: DPA: controller vs processor, telemetry & embeddings — next steps & execution
messages:
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme-legal.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jan 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood DPA — role definitions & telemetry scope

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is Acme's initial DPA redline (ACME_DPA_redline_v1.docx). There are three items we need to resolve before legal can approve:

1) Controller vs. Processor: Acme prefers a controller-controller carveout for any feature where Acme provides end-user intent/context (we flagged a few clauses where we'd like Redwood to accept processor role for standard inference only).
2) Embeddings: we view embeddings as derived data but want explicit prohibition on using customer embeddings to further train or improve models that serve other customers.
3) Telemetry & logs: need tighter retention and a clear list of telemetry categories that are operational (metrics/traces) vs content (full request/response).

Other asks: subprocessors — Acme requests 30 days' notice and a right to object for new subprocessors that access content; cross-border transfer language needs to reference SCCs if data is leaving the EU (noting Acme has EU customers).

Can you confirm Redwood's position on the three bullets and whether you're able to sign via DocuSign? John Park (cc'd on the business side) will want to schedule final signoff once we align.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Lin
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy — Acme Corp

Attachment: ACME_DPA_redline_v1.docx (word doc, redline)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme-legal.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — role definitions & telemetry scope

Sara — thanks and appreciate the clear redline. Quick initial positions from Redwood to make sure we're aligned before legal does detailed markup: 

- Controller/Processor: Redwood's default is to be a processor for inference requests and related stored artifacts (prompts, outputs, embeddings) unless the customer explicitly instructs Redwood to act as controller for model-hosted services. We're open to the "processor for inference, controller carveout" language for the limited hosting case — propose a short definition table in the DPA that maps product features to role.

- Embeddings: We can commit to not using customer embeddings to train models that serve other customers. We do require limited internal use (debugging, quality assurance) on an aggregated basis; propose adding a narrowly scoped "allowed operational uses" clause with hashing/aggregation requirements.

- Telemetry & logs: We segregate telemetry into: (a) operational metrics/aggregates (CPU/GPU utilization, latency percentiles), (b) anonymized traces (no persistent user content), and (c) content-bearing logs (raw requests/responses). By default, content-bearing logs are retained 30 days and only accessible to a small ops crew for incident response; we can offer shorter retention for regulated customers.

On subprocessors: Redwood provides a current subprocessor list and 30-day notice for additions; objection rights are something we typically limit to a narrow set of circumstances (e.g., data residency). Happy to include a 30-day notice + remediation/dispute process.

DocuSign: we're prepared to execute via DocuSign. If Acme can confirm the final redline, we'll circulate our markup and then push to DocuSign for signature routing to contracts@acme.com and aditya.rao@redwood.com.

I'll attach a short markup with suggested language for the embeddings/telemetry bullets later today.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-dpa-markup-20260119.docx (proposed clauses)

From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@acme-legal.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: John Park <john.park@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jan 2026 08:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — role definitions & telemetry scope

Aditya — reviewed your summary with the team. A few clarifications we propose as compromise language (see inline bullets):

- Role mapping table: acceptable so long as the table explicitly lists (i) hosted-model inference, (ii) API calls where Acme provides user content, and (iii) analytics features. We need the DPA to state that for (ii) Redwood is a processor.

- Embeddings: we will accept the "no use for improving third-party models" clause, provided you also add: (a) an audit right for Acme once per year limited to technical evidence that embeddings were not used for model training across other customers, and (b) a clause preventing derivative matching services that would reveal Acme data to other customers.

- Telemetry: Acme's baseline ask is a 14-day retention for content-bearing logs unless otherwise requested. If Redwood needs 30 days for operational reasons, we ask that the DPA provide an option for Acme to select 14-day retention for their account.

- Subprocessors: 30 days' notice OK. For objections, Acme requests a joint remediation period of 21 days; if unresolved, Acme can escalate to seek injunctive relief (legal fallback).

If Redwood can accept the above, we'll finalize and have contracts@acme.com confirm DocuSign routing. Otherwise John and I can set a 30-minute call Thursday to close.

Regards,
Sara

Subject: Re: Redwood DPA — role definitions & telemetry scope

Sara/Aditya — thanks for the constructive back-and-forth. From a legal-execution standpoint Redwood can accept the following consolidated positions: 

• Role table: We'll insert a short "Role Mapping" appendix that maps product features to Controller/Processor status. For clarity: API inference requests where Acme supplies end-user content = Processor. Hosted services where Redwood controls model input/output and determines use beyond request execution = Controller for that narrow use case.

• Embeddings: Redwood will add: (i) a prohibition on using customer embeddings to train models that serve other customers; (ii) an annual technical evidence audit right limited in scope and duration; and (iii) a ban on cross-customer vector-matching features that would expose Acme data.

• Telemetry & logs: Default content-bearing log retention = 30 days. We will add an option for customers to request 14-day retention at account setup or via the Console settings; this will be honored and enforced at the account level. Access controls: content-bearing logs are restricted to incident response ops and required legal requests.

• Subprocessors: Redwood confirms current subprocessor list will be provided in schedule A. We accept a 30-day notice for additions and a 21-day remediation period for objections with escalation paths.

Action items: 
1) Aditya to incorporate the above language into the DPA markup and return a clean redline by EOD Monday.
2) Sara/Acme to confirm DocuSign routing addresses for signature (contracts@acme.com and john.park@acme.com).
3) Legal to prepare an appendix for Role Mapping.

We can then route to DocuSign. Happy to accept execution via Acme's DocuSign envelope so long as we confirm signatories.

- Laura Bennett
VP Legal, Redwood Inference

- Default content log retention = 30 days; Acme may opt into 14-day retention via Console settings at account setup.
